question: Does a stranger with no C compiler get an actionable refusal from `signerd run`?
method: three real trees (published tag v0.2.7 shape, fixed tree), offline, no network; the tarball ships the helper SOURCE and never the binary, so the helper is compiled at runtime

cases.label: read-only install dir
cases.stderr:
grant_file_lease_unavailable: grant_file_lease_unavailable: /usr/bin/ld: cannot open output file /tmp/signerd-lease-measure-Bmk4TE/preB/tools/leasecheck: Permission denied
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status

cases.label: no compiler
cases.stderr:
grant_file_lease_unavailable: the C compiler "/tmp/signerd-no-such-compiler-for-measurement" was not found — signerd builds the lease helper from source, so it needs one
  fix: install a C compiler (cc), or point CC at one: CC=/path/to/cc signerd run ...   # the lease helper is built from tools/leasecheck.c, so the daemon needs a compiler once

cases.label: read-only install dir
cases.stderr:
grant_file_lease_unavailable: the lease helper could not be written to /tmp/signerd-lease-measure-Bmk4TE/fixD/tools — the compiler ran, but that directory is not writable
  fix: make the install directory writable (or pre-build it there: cc -O2 -o tools/leasecheck tools/leasecheck.c)   # the helper must be written next to its shipped source

reason: all verdict fields must hold for the fix to count as measured, not asserted
